mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand but a relative housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 response over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 12-month MA
regime_hint: late-cycle demand slowdown with sector rotation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is less than -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to lower corporate margins and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% on a seasonally adjusted basis, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter indicates a precautionary savings behavior, which historically precedes a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending slows.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS QoQ change > 2% AND GDPC1 QoQ change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2% combined with a consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) annualized increase below 1% for three consecutive months signals an extended period of monetary accommodation and low inflation, which historically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL YoY change < 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is less than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below 50,000 for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a persistent housing downturn, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to construction sector drag.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.
